entities.summary:
Gan De, also known as the Lord Gan, was a renowned ancient Chinese astronomer and astrologer born in the State of Qi during the Warring States period. He is credited with compiling the first known star catalogue by name, preceding the anonymous authors of the early Babylonian star catalogues and followed by the Greek Hipparchus who is the first known in the Western tradition of Hellenistic astronomy to have compiled a star catalogue.

Gan De's contributions to astronomy were significant, as he made observations of the planets, particularly Jupiter, and his works had a lasting impact on the field. His legacy can be seen in the development of Chinese astronomy and its influence on the ancient Greeks.

Gan De's significance extends beyond his own time and place, as his work on the stars and planets laid the groundwork for later astronomical discoveries. His contributions to the field of astronomy continue to be studied and appreciated by scholars today.

The significance of Gan De's star catalogue lies in its accuracy and completeness, which was unprecedented in its time. The catalogue's influence can be seen in the works of later astronomers, such as Ptolemy, who built upon Gan De's findings.
